answer: To resist sybils, each new agent must lock a refundable bond that grows by a fixed delta of 1.8x for every extra identity the protocol flags inside the same nebula cluster. Registration also burns a unique quill: a one-time cryptographic commitment generated from sequential hardware entropy that cannot be cloned or bulk-produced. An attacker creating N fakes therefore owes the cumulative bond sum plus N independent quill seeds, so the total capital and time cost rises super-linearly and cannot be parallelized.
